appraisal_events.evidence: «Vous n'êtes pas de votre temps [...] et je vous en félicite [...] Des efforts tels que les vôtres devraient être encouragés si nous avions un gouvernement.» — «Bloch était flatté de surnager seul dans le naufrage universel.»
appraisal_events.explanation: Norpois singles Bloch out as the one survivor of a general cultural shipwreck, and Bloch takes the compliment at face value. The narrator ironizes it at once by noting that Bloch cannot obtain a single specific point and had never thought himself exceptional, so the praise reads as content-free diplomatic amiability rather than earned esteem.

appraisal_events.evidence: Bloch «ne put arriver à démêler l'opinion de M. de Norpois»; the Zola-trial portrait with sandwiches and coffee «comme au concours général», the «éréthisme nerveux», the supper ordered «sur un ton impérieux qui lui donnait l'illusion du pouvoir»; then his Homeric tirade on Athèna and Picquart, closed by «M. de Norpois ne répondit pas.»
appraisal_events.explanation: The body of the passage comically exposes Bloch as vain, over-excited, and self-deluding, and its final beat has his grandiloquent pseudo-Homeric prophecy met by flat silence. The dominant local movement is his deflation, which cancels the flattery he had just enjoyed.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator's sustained comic portrait — schoolboy provisions at the trial, nervous erethism, the imperious supper giving only the illusion of power — clearly lowers Bloch within this passage.
Bloch cannot extract any answer from Norpois despite repeated probing, and his most elaborate rhetorical performance receives no reply at all; his speech fails to command the exchange.
Norpois keeps full control of the conversation: he flatters without committing, remains undecipherable on the Affair, and ends by declining to answer at all, leaving Bloch exposed.

ambiguities: Whether Norpois's compliment expresses genuine esteem for Bloch's work or is habitual diplomatic amiability that commits him to nothing; the narrator's framing (Bloch can extract no specific content and knows himself unexceptional) supports the second reading, which is why E1 is marked ironized rather than endorsed.

Whether the closing «M. de Norpois ne répondit pas» is a deliberate snub of Bloch, professional reticence about the two officers, or both; the motive is underdetermined, but the deflating local effect on Bloch is the same either way, so it is folded into E2 rather than annotated as a separate snub.
